content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Article III gives Licensor ownership of all Licensed Technology and IP Rights, and the customization/development work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) is captured by that ownership (as enhancements/Derivative Works of the Platform Software). Our only rights are a non-exclusive, Field-of-Use licence that we cannot modify (Art. II(g)) or sublicense/transfer (Art. II(c), Art. VI) and that terminates with the Agreement (Art. XXI). There is also no limit on Licensor's use of data we supply or that it processes for us.

That fails the IP fallback, so I proposed the shortest fallback cure — one inserted clause after the customization paragraph granting a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverables for our business, plus a limitation of Licensor's rights in our data to processing it solely to provide the services. Licensor's ownership of its own platform and know-how is left intact and mapped as already met.
